name: cavemio-code-block
title: Code block
description: Code in an answer: highlighted as it streams, copy and wrap, long files folded, and an optional Apply.

cavemio.usage:
import { CodeBlock } from "@/components/code-block";

<CodeBlock code={code} language="ts" filename="lib/queue.ts" streaming={isStreaming} />
cavemio.accessibility:
- Highlighting runs per line with no dependencies, so it’s instant while streaming. For full grammars, render Shiki output yourself and keep this frame.
- Copy and Wrap are real buttons with labels; Wrap uses aria-pressed. "Copied" and "Applied" are announced from a status region beside each button. The code area is focusable when it scrolls sideways.
- Copy and Apply are Status buttons and the fold label is a Text morph; the CLI installs both. With reduced motion, states change in place.
- Line numbers are hidden from screen readers and from copy and paste.
- The colours follow GitHub’s light and dark palettes; the frame uses your theme’s border and background.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: code
props.description: – · The code so far, or all of it.

props.name: language / filename
props.description: – · Shown in the header. The language also picks the comment style (// or #).

props.name: streaming
props.description: false · Shows the caret and keeps the block open.

props.name: collapseAfter
props.description: 18 · Fold complete code longer than this many lines; 0 never folds.

props.name: onApply / applyLabel
props.description: — / "Apply" · Shows Apply, with progress while the promise runs and "Applied" after.

props.name: highlight
props.description: true · Turn the built-in highlighting off, e.g. for logs.

features.title: Highlighted as it streams
features.description: A built-in highlighter colours each line the moment it arrives, with a caret at the end.

features.title: Copy with feedback
features.description: The icon becomes a drawn check and “Copy” becomes “Copied”. A blocked clipboard says “Couldn’t copy”.

features.title: Wrap and line numbers
features.description: Toggle wrapping, with a line-number gutter that stays put and isn’t copied.

features.title: Long code folded
features.description: Code that arrives complete and runs past 18 lines shows its start and “Show 42 more lines”.

features.title: Apply with progress
features.description: Apply becomes Applying, then Applied. A failure shakes and offers Try again.

features.title: A header that says what it is
features.description: File name and language sit in the header, in colours that follow GitHub’s light and dark palettes.

states.title: streaming
states.description: Lines arrive highlighted, with a blinking caret on the last one. Long code you watched stream stays open.

states.title: complete
states.description: File name and language, a wrap toggle, Copy. Line numbers stay put while you scroll sideways. Toggling wrap eases the block to its new height over 460ms.

states.title: copied
states.description: The copy icon shrinks away through a 3px blur as a check draws itself in 420ms; "Copy" morphs to "Copied", keeping the letters they share, for 1.6 seconds. A blocked clipboard shakes and says "Couldn’t copy".

states.title: folded
states.description: Code that arrives complete and runs past collapseAfter shows its start under a fade. "Show 42 more lines" opens it over 460ms while the fade dissolves and the label morphs to "Show less".

states.title: apply
states.description: Apply → Applying with a spinner while your promise runs → a drawn check and "Applied", as the button eases from your primary colour to a quiet receipt. A rejected promise shakes and offers "Try again". It waits at 40% opacity while code streams, and when the code changes (a regenerated answer) it morphs back to Apply so the new code can go in too.
